QuestionStmt.S: A disc of mass 25 kg and radius 0.2 m is rotating at 240 r.p.m. A retarding torque brings it to rest in 20 second. If the torque is due to a force applied tangentially on the rim of the disc then the magnitude of the force is

Solution.S:
Given: $m = 25$ kg, $R = 0.2$ m, $n = 240$ rpm, $t = 20$ s, $\omega_2 = 0$.

$$\omega_1 = \frac{2\pi \times 240}{60} = 8\pi \text{ rad/s}$$

$$\omega_2 = \omega_1 + \alpha t \Rightarrow 0 = 8\pi + \alpha(20) \Rightarrow \alpha = -\frac{2\pi}{5} \text{ rad/s}^2$$

$$I = \frac{1}{2} m R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 25 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.5 \text{ kg m}^2$$

$$\tau = I\alpha = 0.5 \times \frac{2\pi}{5} = \frac{\pi}{5} \text{ N m}$$

$$\tau = F R \Rightarrow F = \frac{\tau}{R} = \frac{\pi/5}{0.2} = \pi \text{ N}$$

Thus the correct option is C: $\pi$ N.
